sections.h2: Who sends the tax bill in Bartow County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Bartow County Tax Commissioner mails and collects the bill, while a separate Board of Tax Assessors puts the value on your land and house. Payments, mobile home accounts and tax sale overage claims all go to the commissioner's suite inside the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building, 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, Cartersville. The property tax line is (770) 387-5111, and the counter is open Monday through Friday, eight in the morning until five, holidays excepted.

Bartow runs on a sole commissioner form of government. One elected commissioner adopts the budget and sets the millage in a public meeting held at that same building, and the county's own minutes show the 2026 rates were approved on August 5. Cartersville is the county seat. Adairsville, Euharlee, Kingston and Taylorsville hold their own charters, and Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities that still pay through the county office.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, duplicate bills, excess funds forms.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, returns and the notices that carry appeal rights.
  • County Commissioner: adopts the rates and the budget each summer.

sections.h2: What should a Bartow County homeowner weigh before selling?
sections.html:
Bartow sits in the northwest of Georgia, and the Cartersville end of it now behaves like an Atlanta exurb, reached by I-75 more than 40 miles from downtown. The county was carved from Cherokee land in 1832 as Cass County and took the Bartow name in 1861. The Great Locomotive Chase of 1862 passed through, and the Etowah Indian Mounds, the Booth Western Art Museum and Tellus Science Museum still draw visitors today.

Roughly 459 square miles of land stretch from the Etowah River basin to Lake Allatoona and Red Top Mountain State Park on the southeast edge. Drivers use US 41, US 411 and state routes 20, 61, 113, 140 and 293. A house in Cartersville falls under Cartersville City Schools, while most other addresses belong to the Bartow County School District, so confirm the district before you describe a listing to a buyer.

The county's population moved from 100,157 in 2010 to 108,901 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimate for mid-2025 is 120,800. County leaders credit a large industrial base, a battery plant and data center development for the tax digest growth that has let the millage keep falling.

sections.h2: When do Bartow County property taxes come due?
sections.html:
Statements for real estate leave the office around September 15, and the due date is November 15. For 2026 that date was November 15, 2026. Mobile homes follow their own cycle with an April 1 due date.

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the billed party. If you closed on a purchase after that date, phone the tax office and ask for a duplicate in your name, because the first statement went to the previous owner. The county adds that a bill that never arrives does not move the deadline.

  • Online payment sits behind a link on the Tax Commissioner page, and the same page lists qpublic for parcel lookups.
  • Debit and credit cards, whether paid online, at the counter or by phone, add a 2.5 percent convenience charge.
  • A check by mail is made out to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner at the Cherokee Avenue address.

Georgia gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, and delinquent balances can also draw penalties. Ask the office for the figure that applies to your account.

sections.h2: What are Bartow County's 2026 millage rates?
sections.html:
The 2026 rate is 7.11 mills inside city limits and 6.76 mills in the unincorporated county. Last year's figures were 7.40 and 6.87. According to the August minutes, the commissioner chose the rollback rate and noted that rates have trended down since 2013.

A mill is a dollar of tax on each $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is set at 40 percent of what the board calls fair market value. The school board levies its own rate on top, so your statement will show more than the county figure alone. Rather than estimate, ask the tax office for the combined millage tied to your parcel and district.

sections.h2: How do I claim the homestead exemption in Bartow County?
sections.html:
File with the county before April 1, and only for the home where you live. The billing page is blunt that rentals, multi-family buildings and commercial or industrial property are excluded.

The commissioner's August 2026 minutes put the standard exemption at $15,000 of value and say the county is working with the legislature on a move to $30,000 in a future year. Because that is a goal and not a promise, call the office to learn the amount on your current bill. Moving to another Bartow house means filing again for the new address.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Bartow County property value?
sections.html:
Mail a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice date. Georgia sets that window for every county, and it covers disputes about fair market value.

Before any notice arrives, owners may file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating the value they believe is right. Money paid on tax that was wrongly charged can be claimed back within three years of payment, and refunds from a winning appeal are issued automatically. Gather sale prices of nearby houses and dated photos of damage before you write the appeal.

sections.h2: How does a sale interact with the Bartow County tax bill?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax rides with the property, so closing is the moment to settle it. Because the county names the January 1 owner, a seller who held title on that day normally gets the statement even if the deed changes hands in October. Ask whoever handles your closing to show how the year's bill is split and who sends the payment.

When back taxes pile up and the county sells the parcel for more than is owed, the excess is held for the people with a claim. The commissioner's page links an excess funds form for that situation. Selling before a levy usually costs less than waiting, so request a written payoff from the office and compare it with any offer you receive.

faqs.q: When were 2026 property taxes due in Bartow County?
faqs.a: November 15, 2026, with statements mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills are due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the last day to apply for homestead in Bartow County?
faqs.a: April 1. The exemption only covers the home you live in as a primary residence.

faqs.q: How many days do I get to appeal a Bartow assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date the notice was mailed, with the written appeal postmarked inside that window and sent to the Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: Will Bartow County send my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No, statements go to whoever held title on January 1, so ask your lender whether it pays from escrow. A buyer who closed after January 1 can ask the office at (770) 387-5111 for a duplicate statement.

faqs.q: Does Bartow County charge a fee to pay by card?
faqs.a: Yes, 2.5 percent on debit and credit payments, whether made online, in person or by phone. A check by mail carries no such fee.
